open_points.subject: outside material and direct photo access
open_points.text: “Their material stays at a microservice's own intake until the owner or an agent submits it, which is running a flow (`run a flow`) whose operation node takes it from that service — there is no separate submission action” conflicts with “the agent processes a photo itself, outside the kernel, with its own access to the service that holds the photo rather than through the kernel.”
open_points.question: May the agent directly read or process outside-sender material while it is still in the service intake, or must a flow operation first take that material from the intake before any direct agent access?
options: Direct agent access may occur before the flow, so remaining at intake does not prohibit reading or processing
A flow operation must first take the material from intake, after which the agent may access it in another service
Direct agent access is allowed only for material that did not originate in the outside-sender intake
open_points.default_guess: Require a flow operation to take the material from intake before the agent accesses it directly.

open_points.subject: personal-data disclosure boundary
open_points.text: “Personal data — values of class `personal_data` (K-14) reach an agent only as digest and class” and “An agent never receives a `personal_data` value” conflict with “its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns” while agents may access services directly.
open_points.question: Is the prohibition on an agent receiving personal-data content global, including direct service access, or limited to values returned by the kernel surface?
options: It applies only to kernel responses; direct services may return personal-data content under their own policy
It applies globally, so direct service access must also prevent personal-data content reaching an agent
Direct access to personal data is allowed only for the photo-processing case
open_points.default_guess: Treat K-14 as governing only kernel responses, because the new exclusion states that scope explicitly.

open_points.subject: MCP listener and reverse-proxy boundary
open_points.text: “The proxy terminates TLS and is the only client of the kernel's listener, whose address the installation names and which the host does not expose otherwise” gives no check or refusal rule for `mcp_listen_address`, and A17 requires only that the configuration contain an address the proxy reaches.
open_points.question: What makes an MCP listen address acceptable, and is proxy-only reachability a kernel start-time condition or an unverified host precondition?
options: The kernel accepts any syntactically valid listen address and proxy-only reachability is solely a host precondition
The kernel accepts only loopback or local-socket addresses
The kernel verifies or authenticates that every connection came through the configured proxy
open_points.default_guess: Accept only a local listener address, while treating TLS termination and external exposure as host responsibilities.

open_points.subject: K-13 repository discovery
open_points.text: “The repositories are the platform's git repositories the platform manifest names (the manifest's own and each service's)” does not specify where or how the manifest names those repositories, while M28 names only `manifest_location` and `manifest_revision` and A08 defines only service-record lookup.
open_points.question: What manifest facts identify the manifest repository and each service repository so that a second agent can discover them from the named sources alone?
options: A top-level platform-manifest repository map names the manifest and service repositories
Each service record names its own repository and a separate manifest field names the manifest repository
Repository discovery is entirely platform-specific and K-13 is not verifiable by the kernel or these texts
open_points.default_guess: Treat repository discovery as a platform-defined external contract that the kernel neither parses nor verifies.
